solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skin condition is so itchy, unusually, hard inside

indicators.note: done unusually means done in a different way from normal, so the preceding words are rearranged
the hard element is placed within the rearranged letters rather than beside them

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A patient complains that a skin complaint is unusually itchy, with something hard lodged inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself is about a skin condition, so the definition sits in plain view; the letters of 'is so itchy' are scrambled and H goes in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichthyosis is a medical disorder leaving the skin dry, thickened and scaly like a fish's.

clue.text: Catechu fairly embodies this type of plant

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within one's body, so the letters sit inside the run of words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that catechu, a tanning extract, rather resembles some plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Catechu is itself a plant extract, which makes the botanical surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: The chufa is a sedge grown for its edible tubers, the tiger nut, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Auld Nick that is on the phone to America

indicators.note: on here means attached alongside, so one piece is joined directly to the other

blocks.note: in American slang to get on the horn is to make a phone call
i.e. abbreviates Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone on a transatlantic call announces it is the Devil himself speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Auld Nick is a Scots name for the Devil, as is HORNIE, from his horns. 'To America' tells you the phone slang is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Scots nicknames for Satan; Burns uses Hornie in his Address to the Deil.

clue.text: A light snack cheers the old man

blocks.note: ta is British informal thanks, as is cheers
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A light snack lifts the spirits of an elderly father.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapa is a small Spanish savoury dish served with drinks, the singular of tapas.

clue.text: Elated, speaks softly in sound poetic constructs

indicators.note: in sound means judged by how the words are spoken rather than how they are spelt

blocks.note: elated means in high spirits, high
to coo is to murmur gently

explanation.surface: A happy person murmurs gently while reciting carefully built verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Haikus are Japanese verse forms of seventeen syllables, carefully structured short poems.

clue.text: Beat when parading, much troubled with rota

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers on a parade ground are much bothered by the duty rota.
explanation.definitionFit: To outmarch is to march faster or further than someone, beating them on the march.

clue.text: Line of planks to fit out round radius

indicators.note: round means going about the outside, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: to stake, as in grubstake, is to supply someone with the outfit they need
R is the standard abbreviation for radius

explanation.surface: A carpenter is told to fit out a structure around some circular radius.
explanation.definitionFit: A strake is a continuous row of planking or plating running along a ship's hull.

clue.text: Distinguish sailors after end of voyage, dry on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top means placed first, above everything else
end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine
the final letter of the word
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: At the end of a voyage, sailors are told apart, with dry ones on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the sailors behind the last letter of voyage, and 'on top' puts the dry wine above both.
explanation.definitionFit: Secern is a rare verb meaning to discriminate or separate, so to tell things apart.

clue.text: Power put into demonstration not quite in condition

indicators.note: not quite complete means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped
put into means placed inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: a proof demonstrates that something is true
vis is the Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: Political power is slipped into a public protest that does not quite meet a condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' tempts you to write P, but here it is the Latin VIS, which goes into PROO after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or qualifying clause, a condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Stance isn't wobbly, being unimpaired

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and shaken about, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A person whose posture is steady shows they have suffered no injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Intactness is the state of being whole and undamaged, so the condition of being unimpaired.

clue.text: Stop relative leading advance

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this piece comes first in the answer

blocks.note: who is a relative pronoun
A is the abbreviation for advance, as in an advance payment

explanation.surface: A family member is told to halt at the front of an advancing column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' suggests a family member, but it is the grammatical relative pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call telling a horse, or anyone, to halt.

clue.text: Martin's not one breaking window

indicators.note: not here means without, so the named piece is taken away from the word

blocks.note: a follower of Martin Luther is a Lutheran
A is one, and it breaks into the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Martin Luther protests that he is not the one who smashed the window.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin's means belonging to Martin Luther: a Lutheran. Remove the A that interrupts it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A luthern is a dormer window set in a roof, an old architectural term also spelt lucarne.

clue.text: Obscure Scots herb turned up with recipe on pastry crust

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions
a pie is filling inside a pastry crust

explanation.surface: A cook digs out an obscure Scottish herb and a recipe for a pie crust.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the Rx sign on a prescription, from Latin recipe, take.
explanation.definitionFit: Purpie is an old Scots name for purslane, a herb now rarely heard of.

clue.text: Go exercising on range of hills – Americans may get stuck up it!

definitions.text: Americans may get stuck up it!

blocks.note: pep and go both mean energy or vigour
PE is physical education, school exercise
a ridge is a long line of hills

explanation.surface: Hikers training on a line of hills risk getting stuck up there.
explanation.walkthrough: To be up a gum tree is to be in a fix; the pepperidge is an American gum tree, hence the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepperidge, or black gum, is a North American tupelo tree, and being stuck up a gum tree means being in trouble.

clue.text: Soft fabric, small one, mostly costly included

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped
included means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
rich food or furnishings are lavish and costly

explanation.surface: A shopper weighs up a small piece of soft cloth, mostly expensive by the look of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricot is a knitted fabric, fine and soft, used for underwear and dresses.

clue.text: Divine lovely, narcotic tipple, prepared to be imbibed

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk down, so it ends up inside the drink

blocks.note: kava is a mildly narcotic Polynesian drink
prepared and made, as of a meal

explanation.surface: A gorgeous beauty is served a drugged drink that has been made ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine lovely' reads as an adjective and noun for a beauty, but it means a god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamadeva is the Hindu god of love and desire, so a divine being of love.

clue.text: Cub accepts assistance, having debts cleared?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a pup is a young animal, as a cub is
aid and assistance are synonyms

explanation.surface: A young reporter takes some financial help and so clears what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid-up describes someone whose dues are fully settled, with nothing outstanding.

clue.text: Supplier of quips as a point of honour?

blocks.note: a pun is a quip turning on wordplay
a donor supplies or gives something

explanation.surface: A wit makes a matter of pride out of always providing jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The supplier of quips is read as a pun donor, which is then put together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pundonor, from Spanish, is a punctilio, a matter of personal honour or dignity.

clue.text: Like an acid found in Swiss lake limitlessly?

indicators.note: without limits means without its edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: Lake Zurich lies in Switzerland

explanation.surface: A chemist wonders whether some acid occurs in the water of an Alpine lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Uric describes urine and specifically uric acid, a compound found in urine.

clue.text: Super's terribly embarrassed, being under strain

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, with the s
an embarrassed person goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A police superintendent is mortified at being put under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Super is British slang for a police superintendent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pressured is having pressure put on them, so they are under stress or strain.

clue.text: Prince vaunting more of a shower?

blocks.note: first meaning: Prince ... III, long the ruler of Monaco
second meaning: wetter, with more showers of rain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaunting' sets up the pun: a show-er is someone who shows off, as a vaunting prince would.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainier was the name of Monaco's prince, and as a comparative adjective it means wetter, having more rainfall.

clue.text: No longer pays for armed guards king dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so this piece is removed from the word

blocks.note: an armed escort guards a convoy or person
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: The king's armed guards are let go once the money for them runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an archaic word: to escot was to pay for someone's upkeep.
explanation.definitionFit: Escot is an obsolete verb meaning to maintain or pay the reckoning for, so it is a disused sense of pays for.

clue.text: Brevity

blocks.note: the only word printed: the quality of saying things in few words
this is the competition word, which Azed gives with a bare definition for solvers to write their own clue

explanation.walkthrough: This is the Azed competition puzzle: one entry gets only a definition, and entrants send in their own clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Concision is the quality of being concise, expressing much in few words, which is what brevity means.

clue.text: Count calling for more music in opening race (start off)

indicators.note: start off means the beginning is cut away, so the first letter goes
opening here is a verb: the word is opened up to let the other piece in

blocks.note: taken as written
a corso is a race, especially of riderless horses in Italian streets

explanation.surface: A nobleman demands an encore at the start of a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke Orsino opens Twelfth Night with 'If music be the food of love, play on'; Azed calls him Count, as Shakespeare sometimes does. 'Opening' looks like part of the definition but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino's first speech in Twelfth Night asks for more music: 'Give me excess of it'.

clue.text: Like some old Greek wine? Nice to imbibe without limits

indicators.note: without limits means without its outer edges, so the first and last letters go
to imbibe is to drink in, so the other piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A wine buff asks whether a vintage Greek wine would go down well in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Greek wine' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Greek'. Nice wants to be the French city; it is just four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Iastic means Ionian, belonging to the Ionian Greeks or their musical mode.

clue.text: I posed wearing product of indigo

blocks.note: taken as written
a model sits, or poses, for an artist
dressed in clothes means wearing them

explanation.surface: An artist's model sat for a portrait dressed in blue dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red compound obtained by oxidising indigo.

clue.text: Grating sound made by weak horse swallowing bit of straw

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter alone
to swallow is to take inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a rip is a worn-out or worthless horse
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A feeble old horse chewing on straw makes a rasping noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Risp is a Scots word for a rasping or grating noise, as of a file on metal.

clue.text: Vessel trapped in well, causing aggro

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: hale means healthy, well
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: A boat stuck down a well makes trouble for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a water well, but it is the adjective, healthy. Aggro is British slang for trouble or aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle and aggro are both informal words for bother, trouble or harassment.

clue.text: Slow dance, sort of jig filled with love

indicators.note: filled with means having something put inside

blocks.note: a jig is a type of fishing lure
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A slow dance turns out to be a kind of jig full of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jig' suggests a dance in a clue whose definition is a dance; here it is the fishing tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: The loure is a slow French dance in 6/4 time, found in Baroque suites.

clue.text: Gnashers like this will get bent back in twisted irons

indicators.note: bent back means turned to face the other way, so the word is read backwards
twisted means wrenched out of shape, so the letters are scrambled
in means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: sic is Latin for thus, so
taken as written

explanation.surface: Teeth like these get bent backwards when they bite on twisted irons.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnashers is British slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors are the front cutting teeth, which the slang word gnashers covers.

clue.text: Spectacular birds putting little pressure on eggs reared

indicators.note: reared means raised up on end, which in a down entry turns the word upside down
putting one thing on another stacks them, so the pieces are joined in order

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
ova are eggs, plural of ovum

explanation.surface: A breeder gently presses on the eggs of some showy birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavo is the genus of peafowl, the peacocks famous for their spectacular display.

clue.text: Hoo-ha when island bovine's ingested toxic compound

indicators.note: something ingested is taken inside, so these pieces go within the other

blocks.note: a din is a commotion or racket
I is the abbreviation for island
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: There is a fuss when cattle on an island eat something poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Dioxins are highly toxic chemical compounds, notorious environmental pollutants.

clue.text: Position skin design in middle of masses

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letters of the word
in means set inside the other piece

blocks.note: the two central letters of the word
tatu is an old spelling of tattoo, a design on skin

explanation.surface: A tattoo artist positions a design in the middle of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank, a position in society.

clue.text: Become participant in gen? Not I, being out of order (7, three words)

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone denies being the one with the inside information, which is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To get in on something is to join it and take part, becoming a participant.

clue.text: Tip from Scotland as against Ireland?

blocks.note: v is short for versus, against
IRL is the international code for Ireland

explanation.surface: A sports tip from Scotland on the Scotland versus Ireland match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests advice, but it means a metal cap on the end of a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Virl is a Scots word for a ferrule, the metal ring or cap fitted on the tip of a stick.

clue.text: Coastguard's signals worried Scotsmen before once being taken in (10, two words)

indicators.note: worried means agitated and shaken up, so the letters are rearranged
taken in means received inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
or is an archaic word for before, as in or ever

explanation.surface: Anxious Scots on the shore are let in by coastguards giving warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the archaic sense: or used to mean before.
explanation.definitionFit: Storm cones are canvas cones hoisted at coastguard stations to warn shipping of gales.
